analysis" with the raw data download from affymetrix site. A small
bug is the file names in matrix 'pairs' don't match with the file name
which contains suffix "_NSP" or "_STY", therefore
stopifnot(all(getNames(cs) %in% pairs)); or
for (type in colnames(pairs)) {
idxs <- match(pairs[,type], getNames(ces));
sets[[type]][[chipType]] <- extract(ces, idxs);

print(cs);

}
csAccList <- list();

for (type in colnames(pairs)) {

cns <- CbsModel(sets$tumor, sets$normal);

messages.author: 185f4d4fdb048fb8
messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] problem with program in paired "Paired total copy number analysis"
parts:
Hi.

Please let us know what print(csRawList) outputs. Basically, I guess
your CEL files are named something like:

rawData/
Affymetrix_2006-TumorNormal/
Mapping250K_Nsp/
CRL-2325D_Nsp.CEL
...
Mapping250K_Sty/
CRL-2325D_Sty.CEL
...

You have to rename the CEL files by replacing 'all _' (underscores)
with ',' (commas) to have filenames like CRL-2325D,Nsp.CEL and
CRL-2325D,Sty.CEL. The *name* of a CEL file is defined in
aroma.affymetrix as the part of the filename before the first comma
(if any), i.e. with commas both CEL files have name 'CRL-2325D'. All
other parts (except the filename extension) are referred to as *tags*,
i.e. the two CEL files have tags 'Nsp' and 'Sty', respectively. If
you don't replace the underscores with commas, the name pf the two
files are 'CRL-2325D_Nsp' and 'CRL-2325D_Sty' and aroma.affymetrix
will not recognize them as being paired. For more information on this
filename/directory name "grammar", please see Page 'Names, tags, and
filenames' at:

http://groups.google.com/group/aroma-affymetrix/web/file--pathnames-2

In other words, there is most likely no bug. I have updated the
Vignette 'Paired total copy number analysis' explaining this.

You do not have to reran the analysis if you rename the CEL files
under rawData/. Just rename the corresponding CEL files under
probeData/ and plmData/ as well. Most likely you should delete the
files under the cbsData/Affymetrix_2006-TumorNormal/ directory.

Hope this helps

Henrik
